partners.mechanism_chain: GRN (HGNC:4426) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal function (GO:0005740); lysosomal function (GO:0005740) —LEADS_TO→ frontotemporal lobar degeneration (HP:0001297); TP53 (HGNC:11998) —DISRUPTS→ apoptosis (GO:0006915); apoptosis (GO:0006915) —LEADS_TO→ hepatocellular carcinoma (HP:0002671); TP53 (HGNC:11998) —DISRUPTS→ apoptosis (GO:0006915). Loss-of-function mutations in GRN impair lysosomal function, contributing to FTLD. Loss-of-function mutations in TP53 impair apoptosis, contributing to hepatocellular carcinoma. The convergence is through TP53's role in regulating apoptosis, which can be secondarily affected by lysosomal dysfunction or cellular stress resulting from GRN deficiency, and TP53 is also a known causal gene for HCC.

partners.mechanism_chain: GRN (HGNC:4412) —DISRUPTS→ Progranulin processing and secretion (GO:0007225); NCKAP1L (HGNC:28524) —DISRUPTS→ Autophagy-lysosome pathway (GO:0000281); Progranulin processing and secretion (GO:0007225) —LEADS_TO→ Misfolded protein aggregates (CHEBI:36734); Autophagy-lysosome pathway (GO:0000281) —LEADS_TO→ Misfolded protein aggregates (CHEBI:36734); Misfolded protein aggregates (CHEBI:36734) —LEADS_TO→ Frontotemporal lobar degeneration with Tdp43 inclusions (MONDO:0011842); Misfolded protein aggregates (CHEBI:36734) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency with autoinflammation (MONDO:0033551). Loss-of-function mutations in GRN impair progranulin processing and secretion, leading to the accumulation of misfolded protein aggregates (e.g., TDP-43) and subsequent development of FTLD. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in NCKAP1L disrupt the autophagy-lysosome pathway, which is crucial for clearing cellular debris including misfolded proteins. Dysregulation of this pathway also contributes to the accumulation of misfolded protein aggregates, driving autoinflammatory and immunodeficient phenotypes.
